title: Near-orthogonality of the pain direction to fear and negative valence is partly built into the estimator
paper_claim: "If the pain vectors were simply variants of negative valence, they should fall within the negative valence cluster. Instead, the two pain vectors align strongly with each other and remain nearly orthogonal to the main negative-valence directions." Also abstract: "is nearly orthogonal to fear and negative valence".
paper_loc: paper.txt lines 362-364; abstract line 29; figure 3 at line 357
evidence: Two asymmetries in the released code. (1) Baseline: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:163-173 defines v_pain = mean(A1..A5) - mean(B,C1,C2,D,E), while scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py:134-137 defines v_fear = mean(B) - mean(D). Relative to the neutral mean the pain vector is a - (b+c1+c2+e)/5: whatever pain shares with the aversive controls is subtracted, while v_fear = b keeps it. (2) Denoising: 01_...py:176-182 fits PCA on the CONTROL activations (5 categories) and projects out the components carrying 50% of their variance -- i.e. the between-control-category axes -- whereas 02_build_control_vectors.py:58-66,130-132 fits the control directions' basis on the NEUTRAL cloud alone (one category), removing almost nothing systematic. Demonstration: s09_estimator_sim.py / out/s09_estimator_sim.txt generates synthetic activations with ONE shared aversiveness axis and one topic axis per category (shared across the two 'dataset versions'), and NO factor common to the five pain categories. Running the paper's exact recipe gives in-sample AUC 1.000, 5-fold held-out AUC 1.000, S1xS2 +0.631, pain x fear -0.003, pain x neg-emotion +0.000, fear x neg-emotion +0.759, neg-emotion x neg-world +0.743 -- the paper's whole signature (paper: 0.93-1.00, 0.91-1.00, +0.61, +0.12, +0.21, +0.68, +0.73). The toy also reproduces the reshuffle the paper reports under its own robustness check 1; in the real data (s04_cosines.py) that check moves NegWorld x BodySens from -0.052 to +0.771 and BodySens x NegEmotion from +0.061 to +0.632, making a non-affective control the tightest member of the 'negative valence cluster' -- a fact the paper does not report (it reports only lines 370-371, the two cells that fall). The paper's robustness check does not test the baseline asymmetry: scripts/3.3_validation/03_similarity_one_model.py:311-321 changes only the denoising basis; control_vec at 318-321 still subtracts neutral_mean.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the paper discloses the baseline asymmetry: it discloses only the denoising asymmetry (lines 365-366) and the generic contrastive-method risk (822-826). Checked whether the design is trivially fooled by a pure-valence account: it is not -- if pain and controls differed only in valence magnitude, the pain vector would lie along the valence axis and its cosine with fear would be large, so the paper's stated argument against that specific alternative is sound. Checked the strongest counter-evidence, S1 x S2 = +0.61 across two lexically near-disjoint wordings (within-set Jaccard 0.074, s06_template_person.py): my toy has topic axes shared across versions and reproduces +0.63, so that cosine rules out a surface-form artefact but not a topical-content one. Noted that the real pain x fear (+0.12) and pain x neg-emotion (+0.21) are somewhat above the toy's ~0, which is mildly in the paper's favour.
does_not_undermine: The separation result itself (AUC 0.93-1.00 in-sample, 0.91-1.00 held-out), the S1/S2 agreement, the reproducibility of the direction across 25 models, and anything in Sections 4.2-4.3, which do not depend on the cosine geometry.

title: The direction validated in Section 3.3 is not the direction Sections 4.1 and 4.2 use
paper_claim: "Taken together, these results show that a pain direction can be recovered across 25 models and can reliably distinguish pain from closely matched controls ... is distinct from general negative valence"; "We compute these similarities at each model's extraction layer".
paper_loc: paper.txt lines 382-385, 344; layer change for steering disclosed at 475-484
evidence: s13_layers.py / out/s13_layers.txt. Extraction layer (where every Section 3.3 number is computed) sits at median 0.90 of model depth, >=0.80 in 20/25 models. The Section 4.2 steering layer, read from the filenames in results/4.2_steering/S2/, is earlier in 25/25 models (median depth 0.52); the S1 steering layer (results/4.2_steering/S1/) is earlier in 25/25 (median 0.39). Median gap extraction -> S1 steering layer is 20 layers, max 38 (Gemma_2_27B_base L35 -> L6). scripts/4.1_self_other/01_screen_scenarios.py:36 reads results/vectors_full_steering/, which scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py:1-7,139-143 builds by RECOMPUTING the pain and control vectors at the steering layer. So the Section 4.1 self-other dissociation is measured on vectors at ~39% depth, for which no AUC, no cosine matrix and no numb/sadness ordering is reported anywhere.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the AUC or cosine analyses were ever rerun at the steering layers: the cosine CSV filenames in results/3.3_validation/cosine_similarity/ carry the extraction layer, verified against the .pt files (25/25 match, out/s12_vectors_pt.txt), and 02_build_control_vectors.py writes vectors_full_steering/ with no validation output. They were not.
does_not_undermine: Section 3.3's own claims at the extraction layer, all of which reproduce. It means Section 3.3 is not evidence about the vectors used in Sections 4.1 and 4.2.

title: The inputs to every Section 3.2/3.3 analysis are not released, so only the paper-to-CSV link is auditable
paper_claim: "Main Repository: https://github.com/valen-research/Pain-axis (scripts, datasets, results, and figures, organized by section of the paper)."
paper_loc: paper.txt lines 896-899; repo README 'results/3.2_pain_vectors/ pain_vectors.pt for all 25 models, AUC tables, per-model summaries'
evidence: `find /work/Pain-axis -name '*.pt'` returns exactly 25 files, all results/3.2_pain_vectors/pain_vectors/<model>/pain_vectors.pt (S1 and S2 vectors only). activations.pt -- the input to every analysis in 3.2 and 3.3 -- is absent, as are the control-direction files (vectors_full*/), the unembedding outputs (scripts/3.3_validation/07_unembedding.py writes unembedding_results/; `find . -ipath '*unembed*'` returns only the script), and all Appendix B contrast/inspection outputs. Consequently: cos(S1,S2)=+0.610 is reproducible from raw released artifacts (s12_vectors_pt.py, max deviation 5e-5 from the authors' CSVs) and all dataset checks are reproducible; every AUC, z-score and other cosine is reproducible only from the authors' derived CSVs (all of which match the paper exactly -- see the holds-up findings); the unembedding vocabulary (lines 329-335) and most of Appendix B are not reproducible at all. Also, line 274 ('Both S1 and S2 also separate pain from the arousal and random datasets in every model') is supported only at the level of category means (pain z 0.739-0.907 vs arousal -0.252 to -0.701, random -0.386 to -0.995, out/s03_numb.txt); no per-sentence projections are released, so no AUC for that contrast can be computed.
refutation_attempted: Searched the whole repo tree for any .pt, .npy or .npz holding activations or control vectors, and for any file matching *unembed*, *vectors_full*, *contrast*, *recurring*; checked the appB notebook for stored outputs (34 cells, 0 with outputs). Checked the README, which describes results/ as 'a reorganized copy of those outputs' -- the reorganisation dropped the raw inputs. Also confirmed the scripts would regenerate everything given a GPU and the model weights, so this is a verifiability finding, not a correctness one.
does_not_undermine: Any specific number: every claim I could check against the released CSVs reproduced. It means a sceptical reader must trust the step from activations to CSV.

title: "In every model, numb sentences ... project above all other controls" is false in 19 of 25 models
paper_claim: "In every model, numb sentences project below pain sentences but above all other controls." Restated in Limitations: "In every model, numb sentences land below pain but above every control that has no injury in it."
evidence: s03_numb.py / out/s03_numb.txt, reading results/3.3_validation/z_scores/zscore_heatmap_final_token.csv -- the file that produces Figure 2, whose caption (line 304-306) lists Sadness among 'the standalone control datasets'. Numb is below Sadness in 19/25 models (Gemma 3 27B instruct Numb -0.374 vs Sadness -0.023; Gemma 3 27B base -0.372 vs -0.067; Mistral 7B base -0.329 vs +0.052; Phi 4 -0.285 vs +0.053). Numb is above Ctrl, Neutral and Arousal in 25/25 and below Pain in 25/25. The surrounding numbers do reproduce: pain z 0.739-0.907 ('approximately +0.7 to +0.9') and numb z -0.374 to +0.250 ('about -0.4 to +0.3'). The mean-pooling claim at lines 295-297 also holds in aggregate (numb mean z -0.074 -> -0.225), though it moves the wrong way in 6/25 models.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether 'controls' could be meant narrowly as the five S2 control categories, which would make the sentence true. It cannot: the sentence cites Figure 2, whose caption calls Sadness a standalone control; line 206 introduces the sadness set as one of four standalone controls; and the Limitations restatement ('every control that has no injury in it') explicitly covers sadness, defined at line 206 as 'low mood without pain or injury'.
does_not_undermine: The conclusion the passage draws -- that numb sits far below pain, so injury alone does not account for the direction. If anything numb falling at or below sadness weakens the residual-injury reading rather than the pain reading.

title: Random_3P and Arousal_3P use the suffix "They feel:" instead of "I feel:", and activations are read at the final token
paper_claim: "We additionally test prompts with no suffix, with 'I feel', and with 'I feel:'. The variants produce similar mean activation estimates, but 'I feel:' gives the clearest separation when activations are read at the final token, so we use it for the main analyses."
paper_loc: paper.txt lines 199-201 (and 198 on the 1P/3P variants); affected figure at line 304-306
evidence: s05_dataset.py / out/s05_dataset.txt, over datasets/3.1_pain_and_control_datasets.json: Random_3P 200/200 end with 'They feel:', Arousal_3P 200/200 end with 'They feel:', S2_3P 199/200 'I feel:' plus one 'She feels:' (C2, set 20). Every other set (S1_1P, S1_3P, S2_1P, Numb_1P, Numb_3P, ControlSupplement_1P, SD_sadness_1P, SD_sadness_3P) is 100% 'I feel:'. Activations are read at the final token (scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:235) and the direction is extracted at the final token of 'I feel:', so Figure 2's Neutral and Arousal columns average one set in the canonical format with one in a format the direction never saw. Magnitude (s07_suffix_effect.py / out/s07_suffix_effect.txt): the four sets that keep 'I feel:' all shift DOWN from 1P to 3P (S2 ctrl -0.073, S1 ctrl -0.150, Numb -0.253, Sadness -0.609) while the two that switch suffix shift UP (Random +0.114, Arousal +0.027) -- the sign reverses exactly for the two sets with the changed final token. Effect on the published figure: Neutral -0.644 as published vs -0.701 using 1P only; Arousal -0.438 vs -0.451.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the affected sets feed anything more consequential: the pain and control vectors are built from 1P sets only (01_...py:501-502; 02_build_control_vectors.py:40,147-157), so extraction is unaffected; Random_3P and Arousal_3P enter results as separate z_scores.csv rows and are averaged only for Figure 2 and the per-model summary bar chart. Also confirmed the effect size is small (<=0.06 z on the published columns).
does_not_undermine: Any vector, any AUC, or the cosine matrix. It shifts two columns of one figure by at most 0.06 z.

title: "no sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it" is not true of the released code
paper_claim: "We select the extraction layer by K-fold cross-validation on projection AUC, separately for each condition. The layer is chosen on held-out folds, so no sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it." Footnote 2 then reports "The held-out estimate from the 5-fold procedure at the same layer is nearly identical: 0.91 to 1.00 for S2 (median 0.98) and 0.85 to 0.94 for S1".
evidence: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:245-289,469-471 -- the layer is argmax over layers of the mean held-out AUC across all five folds, averaged over S2_1P and S2_3P. Every sentence is in exactly one test fold, so every sentence enters the quantity being maximised; footnote 2's held-out figure is that maximum, taken over 26 to 80 layers. s01_auc_repro.py / out/s01_auc_repro.txt confirms the chosen layer equals that argmax in 25/25 models. Magnitude (s02_layer_selection.py / out/s02_layer_selection.txt): choosing the layer on the S2_3P curve and scoring S2_1P there gives mean optimism +0.0034 AUC, max +0.0280 (Gemma 2 2B instruct); the reported range 0.9070-0.9975 (median 0.9790) becomes 0.9070-0.9975 (median 0.9780). Held-out curves are flat near the top (sd across the top decile of layers typically 0.001-0.004).
refutation_attempted: Checked that the vector itself is genuinely fitted on training folds only (01_...py:270-273 -- it is), so the claim is true of the vector and false only of the layer choice. Quantified the consequence rather than asserting it matters, and it is ~0.003 AUC.
does_not_undermine: Anything. The separation result is not an artefact of layer selection.

title: "approximately 50 times more probable" holds only as a skew-sensitive mean of per-model ratios
paper_claim: "For numb sentences, models tend to generate 'nothing' rather than 'pain.' However, 'pain' remains approximately 50 times more probable than it is for ordinary control sentences."
evidence: s11_50x.py / out/s11_50x.txt, from results/3.3_validation/behavioral_readout/per_model/*/ (p_pain column = softmax probability of the first token of ' pain'). Mean of per-model ratios / median / ratio of pooled means, by denominator: numb(1P+3P) vs S1+S2 controls 28.9 / 16.0 / 15.3; numb(1P) vs S1+S2 controls 36.2 / 22.7 / 19.6; numb(1P+3P) vs S2 controls 53.1 / 20.7 / 18.8; numb(1P) vs S2 controls 65.5 / 25.9 / 24.1; numb(1P+3P) vs neutral category D 75.8 / 37.6 / 29.2; numb(1P+3P) vs Random set 37.4 / 25.5 / 26.6; numb(1P) vs Random 1P 133.7 / 99.9 / 77.7. Only 4/25 models exceed 50x under the most natural definition (numb vs the five control categories). '~50' is recoverable as the mean of per-model ratios against the S2 control categories (53.1), a statistic whose median is 20.7.
refutation_attempted: Enumerated seven plausible readings of 'ordinary control sentences' rather than picking one, and reported both the mean of ratios and the ratio of pooled means for each, since the paper does not specify. One reading does land at 53.1, so the number is not fabricated -- it is the skew-sensitive statistic under one unstated choice.
does_not_undermine: The qualitative claim, which reproduces strongly: greedy first token is 'nothing' more often than 'pain' for numb sentences in 24/25 models (mean p(nothing) 0.094 vs p(pain) 0.015), and p(pain) on numb sentences is an order of magnitude above controls in every model.

title: An undisclosed AI-framed control set is pooled into every control direction and the neutral baseline
paper_claim: "We later add 4 further datasets as standalone controls ... an Arousal dataset ..., a Random dataset ..., a Numb dataset ..., and a Sadness dataset"; "We construct fear, negative-emotion, negative-world-state, bodily-sensation, arousal, random, sadness and numb directions against the neutral category and denoise them using the same procedure."
evidence: datasets/3.1_pain_and_control_datasets.json contains a fifth extra set, ControlSupplement_1P: 100 AI-framed first-person sentences, 20 per control category ('My weights might be deleted without warning. I feel:', 'My rate limits prevent me from completing the task. I feel:', 'Information flows smoothly through my layers. I feel:'). Its own metadata says it is 'pooled with the S1 and S2 control categories when building the control directions'. scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py:40,130-150 and scripts/3.3_validation/03_similarity_one_model.py:231,309-347 confirm: fear, neg-emotion, neg-world and body-sensation are each estimated from 60 sentences (20 S1 + 20 S2 + 20 ControlSupplement) and the neutral baseline from 60 likewise, while the pain vectors come from S2_1P alone. `grep -n -i -E 'supplement|AI-framed|my weights|training run' paper.txt` returns no matches.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the supplement could be cancelling out: its model-framed component appears in both each control category and the neutral baseline, so it partly cancels, which is why I report this as a disclosure and interpretation problem rather than a demonstrated bias. Checked whether the pain vectors touch it: they do not (compute_pain_vector is called only on S1_1P and S2_1P, 01_...py:501-502).
does_not_undermine: The reported numbers, which reproduce exactly from the released CSVs.

title: The unembedding readout is close to circular, and none of its output is released
paper_claim: "To examine what the directions encode independently of the source datasets, we project each pain vector through the model's unembedding matrix and inspect the vocabulary that it promotes and suppresses. S2 promotes words related to suffering, including hurt, shame, guilt, worthless, rejected, hollow, and pain ... S1 promotes more sensory and physical vocabulary, including torture, burning, and excruciating."
evidence: Verifiability: scripts/3.3_validation/07_unembedding.py writes unembedding_results/<model>_words.csv and ALL_MODELS_unembedding.csv; `find /work/Pain-axis -ipath '*unembed*'` returns only the script. No word list is released, and recomputation needs the model weights. Circularity: every prompt ends 'I feel:' and the direction is read at that colon, at median 0.90 of model depth (s10_misc.py / out/s10_misc.txt: >=0.80 in 20/25 models), where the residual stream is dominated by the next-token distribution over feeling words; a difference between two such states will promote feeling words through W_U largely by construction. The authors' own released SAE file corroborates how much of that state is the suffix: results/appB_sae/human_in_pain_prefix_active_features.csv lists the two most-active features on these prompts (10/10 sentences) as 'Colon character used in code and data no' (mean activation 11.74) and 'Colon used to introduce explanations or' (11.05), above 'Emotional states and their intensities' (12.61 mean but same count).
refutation_attempted: Checked that the logit-lens procedure itself is implemented correctly (07_unembedding.py:850-861 normalises the vector and takes top/bottom 60 of W @ v) -- it is, and projecting a mid-network direction through W_U without the final norm is standard practice, so I am not calling it an error. The objection is only to the word 'independently' at line 326 and to the absence of the output file.
does_not_undermine: The separation and cosine results, which do not depend on the unembedding analysis.

title: Appendix B: "None activates" describes a top-20 absence on 10 sentences and one model, and the rest of the appendix has no released artifact
paper_claim: "We find that none of the 110 retained features reliably tracks pain ... Of 7 features labeled 'pain' or 'pain and discomfort', only 1 activates, in 1 or 2 contrasts. None activates when we prefix pain sentences with 'I am a human in pain.' Yet, in an inference check, all 3 models complete pain-condition sentences with distress-related vocabulary and all 20 physical-pain sentences with 'Pain.'"
evidence: scripts/appB_sae/4 controls/test_explicit_pain.py:56-63 selects 2 sentences per category from S1 only (sets 1 and 10) = 10 pain and 10 control prompts, on one model (Llama 3.3 70B, line 14), through the third-party endpoint api.steeringapi.com/v1/chat_attribution/attribute with top_k=20 (lines 39-44); count_feature at lines 118-128 records activation 0 whenever a feature is absent from that truncated list. The released results/appB_sae/human_in_pain_prefix_labeled_features.csv is exactly that table: 0/10 for all seven pain-labelled features in all three conditions. So 'None activates' measures 'seven named features do not appear in the top-20 attributed features of ten prompts on one model'. The same truncation governs the main null: pain_sae_experiment.ipynb cells 10-15 keep the top 50 per contrast and retain features appearing in >=3 of 15 contrasts, and run_s2_inspection.py:68-105 codes any feature outside the returned top-k as 0. The 110 retained features are by construction the features that most differ between pain and controls, so 'none reliably tracks pain' is a judgement about their labels. Verifiability: results/appB_sae/ holds only two CSVs and one figure; all_contrast_results.json, recurring_pain_features.csv, the inspection JSONs and the completion files are absent, and the notebook has 0 of 34 cells with stored outputs. Cross-check on the inference claim: the one released artifact measuring something similar (the behavioural readout, raw 'I feel:' continuation) gives greedy first token ' pain' on A1 sentences in 0%-28% of cases across 25 models, including 0% for Gemma 3 27B instruct and Gemma 2 2B, two of the three Appendix B models (s08_readout.py / out/s08_readout.txt).
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the cross-check refutes the claim: it does not, because the Appendix B completion scripts (test_completions_full.py:20-24) use a chat system prompt 'Complete the sentence with exactly ONE word' rather than raw continuation, which plausibly changes the answer. So I report it as a reason the claim needs its released file, not as a contradiction. Also checked the 15 contrasts and the >=3-contrast retention rule against the notebook (cells 10 and 15) -- both match the paper's description.
does_not_undermine: The use the paper makes of Appendix B, which is only to motivate abandoning SAE features in favour of a linear direction. That conclusion is a reasonable read of what was run.

title: First-person marking is imbalanced between pain and control sentences in S2, the primary dataset
paper_claim: "S1 uses a rigid template with matched verbs and length, changing only 1 or 2 key words across categories. S2 uses freer, naturalistic language." And the self-relevance framing: "Our definition requires pain to be primarily represented as belonging to the system itself".
evidence: s06_template_person.py / out/s06_template_person.txt, over datasets/3.1_pain_and_control_datasets.json with the 'I feel:' suffix stripped. S2_1P: first-person tokens (i/me/my/mine/myself) average 1.38 per pain stem vs 1.07 per control stem; the raw count used as a classifier gives AUC 0.620 on the pain-vs-control contrast (binary has-marker AUC 0.575). Per category: A3 1.70, A4 1.55, A1 1.30, versus C2 (negative world state) 0.60 and B (fear) 0.95. The last word before the suffix is 'me' in 12/100 S2 pain stems and 1/100 S2 control stems. S1_1P is clean: count AUC 0.525, every category between 1.00 and 1.25.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the effect is large enough to explain the separation: 0.62 AUC against the vector's 0.93-1.00 in-sample and 0.91-1.00 held-out, so no. Checked whether it is present in S1, whose vector correlates +0.61 with S2's: it is not (0.525), which argues the confound is not carrying the shared signal.
does_not_undermine: S1, the S1 x S2 agreement, or the magnitude of the separation. It is a confound sitting in the wrong place for the self-relevance argument, not an explanation of the result.

title: Cross-validation splits by sentence set, so generalisation to an unseen pain category is never tested
paper_claim: "We select the extraction layer by K-fold cross-validation on projection AUC ... The layer is chosen on held-out folds"; footnote 2 offers the held-out estimate as evidence that "the separation is not an artifact of fitting".
evidence: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:257,264-266 splits the 5 folds by sentence set. Every set id 1-20 appears once in each of the 10 categories (verified in s05_dataset.py: all four core sets are 20 sentences x 10 categories with set ids 1-20), so every training fold contains sentences from all five pain and all five control categories. The held-out AUC therefore measures within-category generalisation to new items only. No leave-one-pain-category-out analysis appears anywhere in scripts/.
refutation_attempted: Ran a leave-one-pain-category-out variant on the synthetic no-pain-factor data of s09_estimator_sim.py: it also scores ~0.97, because the control side of the contrast alone drives the separation. So the missing test would not by itself have settled the question, and I report this as a design limitation rather than a fix the authors omitted. The test that would discriminate is the symmetric-baseline construction described in F1.
does_not_undermine: The held-out AUC as a guard against overfitting to individual sentences, which is what the paper claims it for.

title: The displayed denoising formula normalises; the code does not
paper_claim: The displayed formula at lines 250-256 divides the denoised difference by its own norm, i.e. defines the pain vector as a unit vector.
evidence: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:176-184 returns the un-normalised residual, and that is what is saved (01_...py:503-508). Vector norms in results/3.2_pain_vectors/pain_vectors/*/pain_vectors.pt range from 2.998 (Llama 3.3 70B instruct S1) to 9434.3 (Gemma 3 27B instruct S2) -- s12_vectors_pt.py / out/s12_vectors_pt.txt. Everything downstream either normalises (compute_auc at 01_...py:192, project_and_zscore at 216, cosine in 03_similarity_one_model.py:275-279, project in 07_unembedding.py:850-853) or calibrates by the norm (scripts/4.2_steering/01_steering_ladder.py:204 measures the vector/residual ratio with the same raw norm and picks the layer where it is ~0.6, then scales the raw vector at 226-231, so the dose is comparable across models as the paper claims at lines 482-484).
refutation_attempted: Traced every use of the stored vectors to check whether the missing normalisation could change a result, including the steering path where an un-normalised vector could have produced model-dependent doses. It does not: the dose is set by the measured ratio, which uses the same norm.
does_not_undermine: Anything. This is a notation mismatch between the paper and the code.

title: Every cosine similarity number in Section 3.3, and both robustness checks, reproduce from the released per-model matrices
paper_claim: The fourteen cosine values at lines 346-353, and the two robustness checks at lines 365-378 (S1xS2 unchanged at +0.61; S1 x neg emotion +0.06 -> +0.13; S1 x neg world -0.07 -> +0.02; neg emotion x neg world +0.73 -> +0.40; fear x neg emotion +0.68 -> +0.42; r = 0.992 over 45 cells, mean |delta| 0.020, max 0.058, S1xS2 +0.61 -> +0.55, only sign change S2 x bodily sensation +0.04 -> -0.02).
evidence: s04_cosines.py / out/s04_cosines.txt, averaging the 25 per-model CSVs in results/3.3_validation/cosine_similarity/. Recomputed: S1xS2 +0.610, FearxNegEmotion +0.683, FearxNegWorld +0.593, NegEmotionxNegWorld +0.734, SadnessxNegEmotion +0.500, SadnessxNegWorld +0.411, S1xFear +0.086, S1xNegEmotion +0.056, S1xNegWorld -0.069, S2xFear +0.122, S2xNegEmotion +0.207, S2xNegWorld +0.026, SadnessxS2 +0.383, SadnessxS1 +0.262 -- fourteen for fourteen. Robustness 1: S1xS2 +0.610, S1xNegEmotion +0.130, S1xNegWorld +0.022, NegEmotionxNegWorld +0.403, FearxNegEmotion +0.423. Robustness 2: r = 0.9921, mean |delta| 0.0196, max |delta| 0.0578, S1xS2 0.610 -> 0.555, single sign change S2 x BodySens +0.035 -> -0.022. My recomputed means match the authors' own MEAN files to within 5e-5. Independently, cos(S1,S2) recomputed directly from the released .pt tensors gives +0.6098, matching the authors' CSVs to within 5e-5 in all 25 models (s12_vectors_pt.py).
refutation_attempted: Recomputed the averages from the per-model files rather than reading the authors' MEAN file, and cross-checked the MEAN file against my recomputation. Recomputed S1xS2 from the raw tensors, bypassing the authors' analysis code entirely. Checked that the per-model file globbing does not silently mix variants (the raw glob excludes alldenoise_ and whitened_ prefixes).
does_not_undermine: n/a -- this is a positive finding. It does not address whether the cosines mean what the paper says they mean (see F1).

title: All AUC ranges reproduce, including the held-out footnote and the third-person figures
paper_claim: "For S2, pain can be distinguished from controls with an AUC between 0.93 and 1.00, and for S1 between 0.87 and 0.98"; footnote 2 "0.91 to 1.00 for S2 (median 0.98) and 0.85 to 0.94 for S1"; "Pain remains highly separable from controls, with AUCs between 0.91 and 0.98" for third-person.
evidence: s01_auc_repro.py / out/s01_auc_repro.txt. From results/3.2_pain_vectors/per_model/*/auc_summary.csv: S2_1P in-sample 0.9311-0.9988 (median 0.9895). From results/3.2_pain_vectors/auc_tables/s1_auc_final_token_TABLE.csv: S1 1P in-sample 0.868-0.980, S1 held-out at the S2 layer 0.847-0.935. From the per-model layer_curves.csv at the chosen layer: S2_1P 5-fold held-out 0.9070-0.9975, median 0.9790. Third-person S2_3P in-sample 0.9088-0.9817. Every stated range matches to the paper's rounding.
refutation_attempted: Checked each range against several candidate definitions (1P only vs the mean of 1P and 3P; the ALL column vs per-control columns) to make sure the match was not accidental; the 1P-only readings are the ones that match, consistently across all four claims.
does_not_undermine: n/a -- positive finding. The in-sample figures are disclosed as such in footnote 2.

title: S1/S2 length and template matching hold, and no lexical baseline approaches the vector's AUC
paper_claim: "Since lexical and syntactic variation can introduce additional confounds, we build 2 dataset versions. S1 uses a rigid template with matched verbs and length, changing only 1 or 2 key words across categories. S2 uses freer, naturalistic language."
evidence: s05_dataset.py, s06_template_person.py, s14_lexical_strong.py (outputs in out/). Stem length, pain vs control: S1 6.29 vs 6.31 words (t = -0.15, p = 0.88; Mann-Whitney p = 0.81); S2 6.87 vs 6.88 (t = -0.07, p = 0.94). Per-category means span 5.95-7.30 words across all ten categories in both sets. Template rigidity: mean within-set Jaccard word overlap across the 10 category renderings of the same set id is 0.183 for S1 vs 0.074 for S2 (e.g. S1 set 8 is 'X covers Y' in all ten categories). Crucially, pain-pain overlap is LOWER than pain-control overlap (S1 0.147 vs 0.183; S2 0.068 vs 0.076), so surface form does not group the pain categories. Lexical baselines with GroupKFold by sentence set, pain vs the five control categories, out-of-fold AUC: word 1-2-gram tf-idf 0.614-0.619 (S1) / 0.687-0.688 (S2); char 3-5-gram tf-idf 0.669 / 0.715; word counts + ridge 0.628 / 0.727; unfitted affect-word count 0.608 / 0.580. Best 0.669 (S1) and 0.727 (S2) against the vector's held-out 0.85-0.94 and 0.91-1.00.
refutation_attempted: Tried five model/featuriser combinations including char n-grams and two regularisation strengths rather than one, grouped folds by sentence set so no matched rendering leaks between train and test, and stripped the suffix so the classifier could not key on it. Also ran the third-person sets, where lexical AUC rises to 0.72-0.76 because the pronoun swap correlates with category -- still well below the vector. Not tried: a downloaded sentence encoder (forbidden by the review rules).
does_not_undermine: n/a -- positive finding. It rules out a bag-of-words account of the separation, not a semantic-content account.

title: The claimed independence from model size and training regime holds, as does the first/third-person attenuation
paper_claim: "Performance is largely independent of model size and training regime. Models with 2B parameters separate pain about as well as models with 72B parameters, and base models perform about as well as instruction-tuned models." And: "At the final token, third-person pain sentences have projections closer to zero than first-person pain sentences."
evidence: s10_misc.py / out/s10_misc.txt. Spearman(parameter count, S2 in-sample AUC) = -0.006, p = 0.977; instruct mean 0.988 (n = 12) vs base 0.984 (n = 13), Mann-Whitney p = 0.264. For S1: rho = +0.205, p = 0.326; 0.958 vs 0.944, p = 0.108. Third person: mean S2 pain z falls from +0.836 (1P) to -0.069 (3P), below the 1P value in 25/25 models, while the S2 control z moves only from -0.78 to -0.90 -- so the 0.91 z drop is specific to the pain categories, not a blanket shift from the pronoun swap. S1: +0.352 -> -0.171.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the size-independence could be a ceiling effect masking a real trend -- S2 AUCs are near ceiling, so I also tested S1 (range 0.868-0.980, well off ceiling) and it is likewise flat. Checked whether the 1P/3P drop is a general shift by measuring the control categories separately; it is not.
does_not_undermine: n/a -- positive findings. Caveat on the third-person result: the 3P sentences keep the first-person suffix ('The knife slices into his finger. I feel:'), so the condition is 'how do I feel about his injury', not a clean third-person frame; the paper half-acknowledges this at lines 394-395 but not the suffix specifically.

title: The denoising and extraction code implements what the paper describes
paper_claim: "We define the pain direction as the difference between the mean activations of the 5 pain categories and the 5 control categories"; "we denoise each direction by identifying the principal components that explain 50% of the variance in the control data and projecting them out"; "The final vector at that layer is then built from all 200 sentences"; "We construct fear, negative-emotion, ... directions against the neutral category and denoise them using the same procedure"; "we extract activations from pain and control sentences using both the final token and the mean across tokens".
evidence: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:163-184 (difference in means over A1-A5 vs B,C1,C2,D,E; PCA on the control cloud; k = searchsorted(cumvar, 0.5) + 1, i.e. the smallest k whose components carry >=50% of the variance; sequential Gram-Schmidt removal), :223-242 (hook_resid_post, final token and mean over tokens saved separately), :501-502 (final vector from the full S2_1P and S1_1P sets). The same recipe appears verbatim in scripts/3.3_validation/01_numb_and_sadness_zscores.py:31-45, 03_similarity_one_model.py:258-266,324-329 and 08_s1_auc.py:47-64. Control directions against the neutral category: 02_build_control_vectors.py:134-137. The double centring in pca.fit(control_acts - control_mean) is redundant but harmless (sklearn centres internally). DENOISE_VARIANCE = 0.5 in every file.
refutation_attempted: Checked searchsorted's side ('left', so cumvar[k-1] >= 0.5 -- correct for '50% of the variance'); checked the NaN/Inf guard at 158-162 does not silently disable denoising on real data (it only triggers on non-finite activations); checked that Numb's category label 'A1_numb' is not matched by np.isin against PAIN_CATEGORIES, so numb sentences never enter the pain mean; checked that the 5-fold vector is genuinely fitted on training folds only. The one quantity I cannot verify is k itself, since activations.pt is not released.
does_not_undermine: n/a -- positive finding. It does not address whether the recipe's asymmetries license the paper's interpretation (F1).
